title: Insight Forge Setup
intro: This wizard is for the installer. You set up one client's Insight Forge from start to finish, inside the client's own accounts. Enter each value once. The wizard keeps it and fills it into every later step. Each client gets its own database, its own app repo, its own AI worker and one login. Steps marked THE CLIENT need the client with you for a few minutes. You can stop at any step - everything you enter is saved in this browser, and you pick up exactly where you left off.

variables.help: Same as in your intake record.

variables.help: The client's own GitHub account. It will own the app repo and the AI worker repo.
variables.pattern_error: Use letters, numbers and hyphens only.

variables.label: Name for your GitHub repo
variables.help: Pick a new name. Example: acme-insight-forge
variables.pattern_error: Use 3-40 lowercase letters, numbers or hyphens.

variables.label: Supabase project ref
variables.help: 20 letters. Find it in your Supabase project URL or Project Settings.
variables.pattern_error: The ref is exactly 20 lowercase letters.

variables.label: Email for your one login
variables.help: Only one person can log in to each Insight Forge.

variables.label: Email address that sends your alerts
variables.help: Must use a domain you verified in your Resend account.

variables.label: Logo URL
variables.help: A public https:// link to the client's logo (PNG, JPEG, WebP or SVG). The app and the image worker both use this exact link.

variables.label: Display font (Google Fonts name:weight)
variables.help: Pick it on fonts.google.com. Use the exact family name, a colon, then the weights.
variables.pattern_error: Use Family Name:weight, for example Lato:400,500

variables.label: Body font (Google Fonts name:weights)
variables.help: Pick it on fonts.google.com. Use the exact family name, a colon, then the weights.
variables.pattern_error: Use Family Name:weight, for example Lato:400,500

steps.title: Before you start
steps.instructions:
Get these ready before step 1. The install takes one working session.

On your computer (Mac or Windows):
- Git: git-scm.com/downloads
- Node.js 22 or newer: nodejs.org (choose LTS)
- Claude Code: after Node is installed, run the command below once.

From the client (they create these, or you create them together with their email):
- A GitHub account (github.com/signup)
- A Supabase account (supabase.com)
- A Claude Pro plan (claude.ai) - THE CLIENT signs in to it once, in the 'Claude sign-in' step
- A Resend account (resend.com) and access to their website domain's DNS
- A Zernio account (zernio.com) and their LinkedIn login - THE CLIENT approves LinkedIn once
- Their logo as a public https:// link, and their two Google Fonts
- Their Business Onboarding Intake record, if they filled one in

Plan the session so the client is with you for the two THE CLIENT steps.

steps.checkbox_label: My computer has Git, Node and Claude Code, and the client's accounts are ready
steps.verify_hint: In a terminal, git --version, node --version and claude --version each print a version number.

steps.title: What this costs
steps.instructions:
Read this first so nothing surprises you later. All prices checked November 17, 2026 - providers change prices, so glance at their pages if it has been a while.

GitHub: $0 on the free plan. GitHub Pages hosts the app for free from a public repo. The app repo holds code only, never client data or keys.

Supabase (your database): $0 on the free tier, 500 MB - plenty for one business. Note: free projects pause after a week with no activity. If that ever happens, reopening the project in Supabase restores it. Their Pro plan ($25/month) removes the pause.

Resend (sends your alert emails): $0 up to 3,000 emails a month, 100 a day. You will send a handful a week.

Zernio (publishes to LinkedIn): your first 2 connected social accounts are free, then $6/month per account. One LinkedIn account: $0.

AI: Claude Pro, $20/month ($17/month billed yearly). This install runs on Claude Pro only. It uses no AI API key and has no per-use AI bill. Your Claude Pro plan writes every draft and every image.

GitHub Actions (runs the AI worker on your GitHub account): GitHub Free includes $12/month of compute. Measured on real runs, one draft uses about 2 cents of it. Set a budget cap in GitHub so it can never bill you past the free amount.

The free tiers above can cover hosting, database, email and the worker. Your one standing AI bill is Claude Pro.
steps.checkbox_label: I know what this costs
steps.verify_hint: No surprises: every later step that touches a paid service links back to this list.

steps.title: Your AI: Claude Pro
steps.instructions:
This system runs on Claude Pro, and only on Claude Pro. The client needs a Claude Pro plan before you start (claude.ai/settings/billing shows the plan). A free Claude account does not work.

No AI API key is used anywhere in this install. The client's Pro plan writes their drafts and images through a worker on the client's own GitHub account. Nothing runs on anyone else's account.

Now copy the block below. Give it to the client to paste into a new Claude chat, or paste it with them. Claude asks six questions, one at a time, and gives back a short business profile plus ready-to-import lines. Keep that answer. The next step imports it.

copy.label: Paste this into a new Claude chat
copy.text: You are helping me set up a content system for my business. Ask me these questions one at a time and remember my answers: What does my business do and who do we serve? What offers or services do we want to be known for? What topics should we never post about? Describe my voice - formal, warm, direct? Who are three peers whose content I respect? How often do I want to post, and at what time of day, in what time zone? When you have all six answers, do two things: (1) summarize them as a short business profile I can keep, and (2) give me my answers as these exact lines so I can import them into my setup wizard: business_name=<my business name>, posting_cadence=<how often I chose>, posting_time=<the time I chose>, posting_timezone=<my time zone>.

steps.checkbox_label: The client has Claude Pro, and I have their business profile
steps.verify_hint: The client's Claude plan page shows Pro, and the chat holds the profile with the import lines.

steps.title: Load your intake answers
steps.instructions: If the client filled in the Business Onboarding Intake for their business, open the Your values box above. Paste their intake record into Import values. Then press Import. This wizard keeps every value and fills it into later steps. If there is no intake record, skip the import and type the name below.
steps.checkbox_label: My business name is saved
steps.verify_hint: Your values shows the business name.

steps.title: Choose your account names
steps.instructions: Each client gets its own GitHub repo and its own Supabase project. Nothing is shared between clients. Type the client's GitHub username and pick a name for the new app repo.
steps.checkbox_label: Both names are saved
steps.verify_hint: Your app address in Your values shows https://...github.io/... with your names.

steps.title: Create your empty repo
steps.instructions:
Sign in to GitHub as the client. Create a new empty repo named {{repo_name}}. Set it to Public. Do not add a README or other files.

Why Public: GitHub Pages hosts the app for free only on public repos. The repo holds app code only. The client's data and keys live in Supabase, never in this repo.
steps.checkbox_label: The empty repo exists
steps.verify_hint: The address opens and says the repo is empty.

steps.title: Copy the app code
steps.instructions: Run these commands on your computer. They copy the Insight Forge code into your repo, then switch to the repairs branch, which holds the fixes from the November 2026 install test. The code has an old .env file inside. The commands remove it. They also remove the setup-wizard folder.

copy.label: Terminal commands

steps.checkbox_label: The commands ran with no error
steps.verify_hint: Run: git status. It shows .env as deleted and the branch as install-test-repairs-2026-11-18.

steps.title: Set your app path
steps.instructions: The app uses the repo name in its web path. Replace the old name in two files. On a Mac, use sed -i '' instead of sed -i.

copy.label: Terminal commands (run inside the folder)
copy.text:
sed -i 's#/knowledge-loom-prismm/#/{{repo_name}}/#' vite.config.ts
sed -i 's#basename="/knowledge-loom-prismm"#basename="/{{repo_name}}"#' src/App.tsx
grep -rn "knowledge-loom-prismm" vite.config.ts src index.html public

steps.checkbox_label: The last command printed nothing
steps.verify_hint: If grep prints a line, replace the old name with {{repo_name}} in that file.

steps.title: Create your Supabase project
steps.instructions: In your own Supabase account, create a new project for {{business_name}}. Choose a strong database password and keep it in your password manager. Do not type it here. When the project opens, copy the project ref from its web address. It is the 20 letters before .supabase.co. Free tier note: a free project pauses after a week with no activity. A weekly posting schedule keeps it active; their Pro plan ($25/month) removes the pause. This is already on your cost list.
steps.checkbox_label: The project ref is saved
steps.verify_hint: Your values shows your Supabase project URL. It opens a page from Supabase.

steps.title: Turn on database extensions
steps.instructions: In Supabase, open Database, then Extensions. Turn on pg_cron and pg_net. The daily jobs need them. If a later step shows an error about cron or net, come back here first.
steps.checkbox_label: Both extensions are on
steps.verify_hint: Both show as enabled.

In your repo, open Settings, Secrets and variables, Actions. Add three repository secrets with these exact names. For the publishable key, open Supabase, Project Settings, API Keys. Copy the publishable key into GitHub only.

Then open the Variables tab on the same page. Add one repository variable. It turns on images in the app.

steps.instructions: Run these commands in your repo folder. The push starts the build.

copy.label: Terminal commands

git commit -m "Set up Insight Forge for {{business_name}}"
git branch -M main
git push -u origin main

steps.title: Create your one login
steps.instructions: In Supabase, open Authentication, Users, then Add user. Use the email below and set a password in Supabase. Then open Sign In / Providers and turn off Allow new users to sign up. Then open URL Configuration and set Site URL to your app address.
steps.checkbox_label: The user exists and sign up is off
steps.verify_hint: You can log in at {{app_url}} with {{login_email}}.

steps.title: Enter your brand
steps.instructions:
Log in to the app as the client. Open Settings and Strategy. Enter the brand values below, and the long fields (description, audience, tone, words to avoid) from the intake record. Do not import Prismm content.

Still in Strategy, create at least one format, one nature, and one job for the client. These start empty on every new install; the app saves what you enter here and uses it for drafts, prompt previews, and the schedule. No database work is needed - type them in the Strategy page.

Then open Visual Studio. Set the logo URL to exactly {{logo_url}}, and the display and body fonts to the family names in {{display_font}} and {{body_font}}. Press Save. The image worker uses these same values.

steps.verify_hint: Settings shows your business name and colors.

steps.title: Copy the AI worker to the client's GitHub
steps.instructions:
The worker is the part that writes drafts and images with the client's Claude Pro plan. It runs on the client's GitHub, not on anyone else's account.

Signed in to GitHub as the client, open the import page below. In 'Your source repository's clone URL', paste the source address. Owner: {{github_username}}. Repository name: insightforge-worker. Choose Private. Press Begin import and wait for 'Import complete'.

Why Private: the worker's run logs belong to the client.
steps.checkbox_label: The import is complete and the repo is Private
steps.verify_hint: https://github.com/{{worker_repo}} opens and shows the folders .github, render and scripts.

steps.title: THE CLIENT: Claude sign-in
steps.instructions:
The client must do this part. It creates a sign-in token for the client's own Claude Pro plan. No API key is involved.

1. On your computer, run the command below.
2. A browser page opens. THE CLIENT signs in with their own Claude Pro account and approves.
3. The terminal shows a long token. Leave the terminal open. You paste the token in the next step, inside GitHub only.

Write down today's date. The token lasts one year (Anthropic's authentication guide, checked November 17, 2026).
steps.checkbox_label: The client signed in and the terminal shows the token
steps.verify_hint: The terminal shows a token and no error.

steps.title: Make the two setup tokens
steps.instructions:
The connect button in a later step needs two tokens. You make them in the client's accounts and paste them into GitHub only.

Token 1 - GitHub (signed in as the client): open the first link. Name: insightforge-setup. Expiration: 1 year. Repository access: Only select repositories, then {{worker_repo}}. Permissions: Contents: Read and write. Secrets: Read and write. Actions: Read-only. Nothing else. Press Generate and keep the token on screen.

Token 2 - Supabase (signed in as the client): open the second link. Press Generate new token. Name: insightforge-setup. Keep the token on screen.

Why: the connect button uses these to store the matching secrets on both sides by itself, so you never handle the secrets.
steps.checkbox_label: Both tokens are on screen
steps.verify_hint: GitHub shows the new token once. Supabase shows the new token once.

steps.title: Paste the three tokens into the worker repo
steps.instructions:
Open the worker repo's secrets page below. Press New repository secret three times, once per row. Paste each token as the value. Use these exact names.

This is the only place the tokens go. Never paste them in this wizard, an email or a chat.

copy.label: Name for the Claude token (from the Claude sign-in step)

steps.checkbox_label: The worker repo lists all three secrets
steps.verify_hint: The secrets page lists CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, SETUP_GH_TOKEN and SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN.

steps.title: Press the connect button
steps.instructions:
Open the connect page below. Press Run workflow. Fill in the five boxes with the values below, then press the green Run workflow button. It takes about 3 minutes.

What it does: it bundles the logo and fonts for the image worker, makes every connection secret, and stores them in the worker repo and in Supabase. Nobody sees the secrets.

If the run fails, open it. The red line says what to fix, for example a missing token or a font name. Fix it and run it again. Running it again is safe.

copy.label: token_date (the Claude sign-in date, YYYY-MM-DD; empty = today)

steps.checkbox_label: The connect run is green
steps.verify_hint: The run shows a green check, and its summary says 'Connected' with the renewal date. Write that date down.

steps.title: Set the GitHub budget cap
steps.instructions:
Signed in to GitHub as the client, open the budgets page below. Press New budget. Product: Actions. Amount: $0. Turn on 'Stop usage when budget limit is reached'. Save.

Why: GitHub Free includes $12 a month of compute for the worker. Measured on real runs, one draft uses about 2 cents. The cap makes sure GitHub can never bill the client for more.
steps.checkbox_label: The $0 Actions budget with stop-usage is saved
steps.verify_hint: The budgets page lists Actions, $0, stop usage on.

steps.title: THE CLIENT: Connect publishing
steps.instructions:
Publishing runs through Zernio.

1. In the client's Zernio account, open the API keys page and create a key.
2. Run the command below in your terminal, with PASTE_YOUR_ZERNIO_KEY replaced by that key. Never paste the key in this wizard.
3. In the app, open Settings and press the connect button for LinkedIn. THE CLIENT signs in to LinkedIn and approves.
steps.checkbox_label: The Zernio key is set and LinkedIn shows as connected
steps.verify_hint: Settings shows each channel as connected.

steps.title: Test one draft and one image
steps.instructions:
1. In the app, create one draft. It appears in Review within a few minutes.
2. Approve it. Its image appears a few minutes later.
3. Open Visual Studio and press Generate preview. A preview appears.

Each one is a run on the worker's Actions page below. A green run is a success. If a run is red, open it: the last job names the stage that failed and never shows a secret.

If Visual Studio has no saved brand config yet, the image renders unbranded on purpose. Save the brand config in step 19 first to get the client's mark.
steps.checkbox_label: A draft, its image and a preview all appeared
steps.verify_hint: Three green claude-loom-worker runs on the worker's Actions page.

steps.title: Run the health check
steps.instructions: Open the health check page. Fix any red item, then reload.
steps.checkbox_label: All checks are green
steps.verify_hint: Every line shows OK.

steps.title: Set the renewal reminder
steps.instructions:
The Claude sign-in lasts one year. The connect run's summary shows the exact renewal date.

Set a calendar reminder two weeks before that date, and write down who owns the renewal.

To renew: THE CLIENT repeats the Claude sign-in step. Paste the new token over CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN on the worker secrets page. Make new setup tokens if they expired. Then press the connect button again with the new date.

A reminder lowers the chance of a silent stop - it cannot prevent one.
steps.checkbox_label: Renewal reminder set and owner written down
steps.verify_hint: A reminder exists two weeks before the renewal date, and the renewal owner is named.
